author: reek
body: Two functions with identical bodies whose parameters are declared in opposite orders. Both count the elements of a list and both must answer three. The only difference between them is whether the declaration order matches the order the body first reads the parameters in.

author: reek
body: e-bound declares the accumulator first and reads the list first. e-swap declares the list first and reads the list first.

author: reek
body: On x86-64 both answer three. This file is the control and the probe: run it here, then cross-compile it and disassemble, and compare the prologue's parameter binding against the registers the loop body actually reads.
